lifecycle.creation_reason: MT-158 residuals: GET /jobs, GET /jobs/:id, POST /jobs/:id/cloud_escalation/consent and non-Locus job kinds were unauthenticated and root-run; resume read the job as root; wp_id/mt_id/iteration_id/dependency_id were global keys, so a second account's create revealed the first account's ids.

closure_unit.outcome: Every /jobs route and every job kind requires the account session and reads or writes jobs as that account's record user; a job the caller cannot see answers exactly like an unknown id. Locus work packet, microtask, iteration and dependency ids are owner-scoped, so the same id created by two accounts never collides and no response reveals another account's ids.

specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: 6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary.

- root, system, namespace-owner, database-owner, and other privileged SurrealDB sessions MUST NOT execute ordinary protected-resource flows or count as privacy/isolation proof because privileged users bypass table permissions;

Application authorization remains required for action semantics and capability checks; record-user table/field permissions plus ResourceBroker are the non-bypassable product data boundary, not the only policy layer.

**[LM-RLS-001]** Multi-user workspace isolation MUST use authenticated record-user table/field permissions intersected with ResourceBroker scope. A `viewer` can read but not create/edit LoomBlocks; a `member` can create and edit; an `admin` can delete and manage workspace settings.

**[LM-RLS-002]** Authority tables default to `PERMISSIONS NONE`; every grant is explicit at the database layer and rechecked by ResourceBroker. Privacy proof MUST execute as authenticated record users because root, namespace, database, and other system users bypass record-user table permissions.

Every durable or derived ProtectedResource MUST carry, directly or through a canonical registry row: [...] - `owner_account_id`, `created_by_principal_id`, `created_in_session_id`, and current `access_space_id` or explicit Space links;

7. Denials MUST use constant-shape responses where practical so counts, identifiers, names, paths, thumbnails, timing, search facets, error variants, logs, or diagnostics do not reveal that a restricted resource exists.
1. Default visibility is private to the owning LocalAccount until an explicit ResourceGrant says otherwise.

materialized_acceptance.text: POST /jobs for EVERY job kind requires the account session and a named workspace (workspace_id, or job_inputs.workspace_id / job_inputs.wsid), authorized with fs.write + Create BEFORE any table access; the job is created and started under that account's record-user scope (MT-158 / api/bundles.rs pattern). A doc_id is resolved only under that scope and must belong to the named workspace. Anonymous, workspace-less, foreign-workspace or foreign-document requests get the constant 403 and create no ai_jobs row. Spec: 02:2758: "6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary."

GET /jobs and GET /jobs/:id require the account session and read ai_jobs as the record user (fn::mt154_job_access): the list holds only jobs of workspaces the caller can read; a job of another account and an unknown id both get the identical constant 403. Spec: 02:2759: "7. Denials MUST use constant-shape responses where practical so counts, identifiers, names, paths, thumbnails, timing, search facets, error variants, logs, or diagnostics do not reveal that a restricted resource exists."

POST /jobs/:id/resume and POST /jobs/:id/cloud_escalation/consent resolve the job as the record user (invisible or unknown -> the same constant 403), re-authorize the job's workspace (fs.write + Update) and run the resume / consent write under that scope; a job with no single workspace ref is denied. Spec: 02:2773: "- root, system, namespace-owner, database-owner, and other privileged SurrealDB sessions MUST NOT execute ordinary protected-resource flows or count as privacy/isolation proof because privileged users bypass table permissions;"

Locus ids are owner-scoped (D-154-3 extension). A record user's work_packets / micro_tasks / mt_iterations / dependencies rows are keyed [owner_scope, id] with owner_scope = fn::mt158_dependency_graph_scope() ('account:<id>'); root/system rows keep their plain id. The id fields assert the id component of the record key; uniqueness indexes become (owner_account_id, id); record-user create requires the record key's owner component to be the caller's own scope. The same wp_id/mt_id/dependency_id created by two accounts yields two independent rows. Spec: 02:2752: "1. Default visibility is private to the owning LocalAccount until an explicit ResourceGrant says otherwise." 02:2759: "7. Denials MUST use constant-shape responses where practical so counts, identifiers, names, paths, thumbnails, timing, search facets, error variants, logs, or diagnostics do not reveal that a restricted resource exists."

No Locus response reveals another account's ids: a create of an id another account owns succeeds for the caller (its own row); reads through the Locus routes answer 404 identical to a missing id for ids the caller does not own. Spec: 02:2759: "7. Denials MUST use constant-shape responses where practical so counts, identifiers, names, paths, thumbnails, timing, search facets, error variants, logs, or diagnostics do not reveal that a restricted resource exists." LM-RLS-001: "**[LM-RLS-001]** Multi-user workspace isolation MUST use authenticated record-user table/field permissions intersected with ResourceBroker scope. A `viewer` can read but not create/edit LoomBlocks; a `member` can create and edit; an `admin` can delete and manage workspace settings."

engine_facts: SurrealDB is pinned =3.2.0 (src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml). Facts verified in surrealdb-core-3.2.0 source by the authority matrix:

F1 Table and field permissions are OFF inside a PERMISSIONS predicate (dbs/options.rs:201 new_for_permission_predicate; doc/check.rs:457-470; exec/permission.rs:87-99). Predicates and the fn::* functions they call see every row and field, including fields that are FOR select NONE.

F2 A top-level query issued on a record-user connection DOES enforce field permissions. Never probe a predicate by running `RETURN fn::...` directly as the record user; it reads permission-hidden fields as NONE and lies. Probe inside a predicate instead (e.g. a probe table whose PERMISSIONS FOR select calls the function).

F3 A denied CREATE, UPDATE or DELETE is SILENTLY IGNORED: no row returned, no error (doc/check.rs:457,469 IgnoreError::Ignore). Every record-user write MUST check the returned row (or a follow-up SELECT) and map an empty result to the constant denial; the failure otherwise surfaces later as a field ASSERT 500, an empty 404, or a guard THROW 403.

F4 REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE/UNSET and DEFINE EVENT bodies run with permissions OFF (doc/purge.rs:376,385; doc/event.rs:52,80). Cascades are never blocked by the caller's delete permission, and cascade targets need no delete predicate for the cascade itself.

F5 Session selection: `SurrealStorage::with_record_user_scope(scope, fut)` (src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal.rs:956 @ab618f46) sets a tokio task-local; `with_data_operation` then signs a cloned client in as the record user. Anything outside that scope, INCLUDING work moved into `tokio::spawn`, runs as root. Re-enter the scope inside every spawned future that touches protected tables.
authority_toolkit: Rust authorization entry points (all @ab618f46, src/backend/handshake_core/src/): `api::authority::authorize_request(state, headers, capability_id, ResourceKind, external_resource_id, ResourceAction)` (api/authority.rs:1216) returns an AuthorizedResourceContext whose `.record_user_scope` MUST then wrap the storage call via `state.surreal.with_record_user_scope(ctx.record_user_scope, fut)`. A route that calls authorize_request but writes outside that scope is still ROOT-WRITE.

`api::authority::require_authenticated_session` (api/authority.rs:1013) is the axum route_layer middleware C2 used for process-starting routes with no protected-resource row (see api/debug_adapter.rs:183-186 route_layer). `authenticated_session_credentials` (api/authority.rs:1031) returns the LocalSessionContext + token + channel binding hash. Missing/invalid credentials map to `constant_denial()` = 403 {"error":"HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE"}.

schema_repin_procedure: Schema re-pin procedure (the one C2 used for MT-109 remediation_v24 and C3 is using now): (1) Batch every schema edit for this MT first. Edit `src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/schema.surql` (the live schema for a fresh store). (2) For every changed statement add a (current_text, predecessor_text) pair to a delta array in `schema.rs` next to `MT109_C2_SCHEMA_DELTAS` (schema.rs:1991 @ab618f46) so predecessor reconstructions revert it and upgrades re-emit it from SCHEMA; the pair must be byte-exact (scripts in ../Handshake_Artifacts/WP-KERNEL-012/MT-109/kb-c2/scripts/strip_check.js show how C2 proved a revert is exact). (3) Build the lib once, then run ONE pin-measure run of the pin tests (check PIN-MEASURE). It is expected to fail and prints the new values: MT109_LOOM_CATALOG_SHA256=, MT109_CURRENT_AUTHORITY_INFO_SHA256=, MT109_PREDECESSOR_AUTHORITY_INFO_SHA256=, MT139_CURRENT_SCHEMA_INFO_SHA256=, EXPECTED_ATELIER_CATALOG_SHA256= and the `left:` values of the GENERATED/DECLARATIVE assertions. minimum_controls: Every positive proof runs as an authenticated record user (account session + channel binding). A root/admin session (with_admin_operation, test_admin_query*, SurrealStorage without with_record_user_scope) may only SEED preconditions that the product itself cannot create, and never counts as privacy/isolation proof (02:2773, LM-RLS-002).

Denied writes are proven by re-reading the canonical row after the call (F3: denied writes are silent). A 403 status alone is not proof that nothing was written.
